newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa bans manufacture of anti-personnel mines.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa bans manufacture of anti-personnel mines.

text.p: South African Defence Minister Joe Modise announced on Thursday the country had banned the manufacture of anti-personnel mines as part of international efforts to rid the world of the weapon.

Modise told a news conference that President Nelson Mandela's cabinet had taken the decision on Wednesday and the country's stockpile of 160,000 anti-personnel mines would be destroyed as soon as possible.
"Cabinet decided on a total prohibition on the use, development, production and stockpiling of anti-personnel landmines with immediate effect," he said.

Modise said South Africa fully endorsed the view of the International Committee of the Red Cross that "the limited military utility of anti-personnel mines is far outweighed by the appalling humanitarian consequences of their use".
"In adopting this position, the South African government is reinforcing efforts to bring about a universal ban on these mines and their complete elimination," Modise said.
He said 2,000 people worldwide were killed or maimed every month by this type of mine, thousands of which are still scattered in South Africa's regional partners Angola and Mozambique.
Modise said South Africa would continue to research so- called "smart" mines which automatically render themselves inert after a given time.
"Our people can study it and know how to deal with it when we come across it, but we will not allow the production of smart anti-personnel mines," he said.
Modise said Scandinavian countries had also banned production of anti-personnel mines, but countries like Britain, France and the United States regarded them as a necessary defensive measure.
Asked why he had pushed for a ban, Modise replied:
"Have you been to Angola? Have you seen those people who have been amputated by those mines? It hasn't stopped, it's still going on. People can't even begin to reorganise their lives."
